Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.2.4, PDF p.54

10.3.2.4 STM state order conditions table applicable to STM X, associated to Level NTC X (ERTMS/ETCS on-board STM Control Function) Condition Content of the conditions Id A1 (STM X connects to the STM Control Function) AND (STM X reports PO state) A2 (“Request CO state” received from STM X)

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.54

3.2.0 FFFIS Condition Content of the conditions Id A3 (“Request DE state” received from STM X) AND (ETCS Train Data is validated) A4a (“Request CS state” received from STM X) (ERTMS/ETCS on-board performs a level transition ordered by the trackside from Level NTC B4a X to Level 0, 1, 2, 3) C4a (announcement for a transition to Level NTC X is stored) AND (STM X reports HS state) AND (a level transition order to Level NTC Y is received before the transition to Level NTC X) AND (STM X is different from the STM Y associated to Level NTC Y) B4b (The driver manually changes the level from Level NTC X to Level NTC Y) AND (STM X is different from the STM Y associated to Level NTC Y) E4a (ETCS mode changes to SB) G4a (STM X reports “HS state”) AND (no transition to any level associated to STM X for further location is stored on-board) AND (Override function is not active) AND (ETCS level is different from any level associated to STM X) H4a (ETCS mode is SB) AND (No cab is active) I4a (ETCS mode changes to SH) J4a (announcement for a transition to Level NTC X is stored) AND (STM X reports HS state) AND (a level transition order to Level 0, 1, 2 or 3 is received before the transition to Level NTC X) K4a (The driver manually changes the level from Level NTC X to Level 0, 1, 2 or 3) L4a (ETCS mode changes to TR) A4b (ERTMS/ETCS on-board performs a transition ordered by the trackside from Level NTC X to Level NTC Y) AND (STM X is different from the STM Y associated to Level NTC Y) A6 (A transition to Level NTC X for a further location is stored on-board) AND (STM X reports CS state) AND (no other STM reports HS state) B6 (ETCS mode is SB) AND (Cab is active) AND (valid level of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board is Level NTC X) AND (STM X reports CS state) AND (no other STM reports HS state) A9 (level of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board is Level NTC X) AND (STM X reports CS or HS state) AND (no other STM reports DA state) AND (ETCS mode is SN, SL or NL) A15 (the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is NOT powered) A16 (the STM Control Function receives from STM X a state request which is not allowed by the state transition table) B16 (STM X reports a state it must not be in according to table 9.2.1.1) C16 (the STM Control Function has sent a state transition order except “DA state transition order” and except “conditional CS state transition order”) AND (STM X does not report the required state within a maximum delay time of 10 seconds)

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.55

3.2.0 FFFIS Condition Content of the conditions Id D16 (the STM Control Function has sent a “DA state transition order”) AND (STM X does not report the required state within a maximum delay time of 5 seconds) E16 (the STM Control Function has sent a “conditional CS state transition order”) AND (STM X does not report CS state or send a “National Trip Procedure” information within a maximum delay time of 10 seconds) F16 (the STM Control Function has sent a “conditional CS state transition order”) AND (the STM Control Function has already received a “National Trip Procedure” information from STM X) AND (STM X does not report CS state or send a “National Trip Procedure” information within a maximum delay time of 10 seconds) H16 (a final disconnection between the ERTMS/ETCS on-board STM Control Function and STM X was detected (see [3] and [2])) I16 (The ERTMS/ETCS on-board performs a transition ordered by trackside to Level NTC X) AND (STM X is not available) L16 (STM X has not yet sent the Specific NTC Data Need) AND (STM X requests CO state) N16 (The timeout TrainDataView_STM_Response_Timeout for STM X has expired) O16 (The timeout TrainDataEntry_STM_Response_Timeout for STM X has expired) P16 (A safety-related information has not been transmitted to STM because of disconnection) Q16 (“National Trip Procedure” is active) AND (STM X reports again “National Trip Procedure” information) AND (the current ETCS mode is PT or UN) A17 (STM X reports FA state)

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.2.5, PDF p.56

10.3.2.5 Note: The delay is shorter for transition to DA state because this transition is assumed as the most critical one from a safety aspect.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.2.6, PDF p.56

10.3.2.6 When the conditions to change the STM state within the STM Control Function are valid according to 10.3.2.2 and 10.3.2.4, the STM Control Function shall send the corresponding state transition order to STM X.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.2.6.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.2.6.1, PDF p.56

10.3.2.6.1 Exception 1: The STM Control Function shall not send an order for NP or PO state.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.2.6.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.2.6.2, PDF p.56

10.3.2.6.2 Exception 2: The STM Control Function shall not send an order for FA state if the STM has reported FA state (transition A17).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.2.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.2.7, PDF p.56

10.3.2.7 When the state transition order is going to CS state, the STM Control Function shall send an “unconditional order CS state” for the transitions A4a, B4a, C4a, E4a, G4a, H4a, I4a, J4a, K4a and L4a, and a “conditional order CS state” for the transitions A4b and B4b.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.2.8

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.2.8, PDF p.56

10.3.2.8 Note about Q16 condition: The Trip mode is entered if the STM X is in National Trip Procedure when a transition to level 0, 1, 2 or 3 occurs. The National Trip Procedure

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.56

3.2.0 FFFIS may still be reported after this transition in case the STM has been ordered to CS with a conditional order due to a previous level transition from NTC X to NTC Y.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3, PDF p.57

10.3.3 Requirements linked to state transition orders and state reports

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.1, PDF p.57

10.3.3.1 The STM Control Function shall not evaluate the state transition order conditions, except conditions to FA state, if this STM has not reported the state corresponding to the last state transition order.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.2, PDF p.57

10.3.3.2 An STM is considered as active by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board from the moment it has sent the DA state order to the STM until it sends another state order to this STM (except “conditional CS state transition order”) or receives a state report different from DA from this STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.3, PDF p.57

10.3.3.3 The STM Control Function shall command the emergency brake from the moment a “conditional CS state transition order” has been sent to a STM and this STM is in National Trip Procedure, up to the moment this STM reports CS state, or is considered as failed and the train reaches standstill.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.3.1, PDF p.57

10.3.3.3.1 Note: This brake command avoids that the train could run untimely without supervision, in case the active STM does not send a brake command but still sends its National Trip Procedure which delays the activation of the STM of the newly entered area.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.4, PDF p.57

10.3.3.4 The STM Control Function shall apply the emergency brake when the level is NTC X and the mode is SN and STM X is known as installed on-board but not available.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.5, PDF p.57

10.3.3.5 Exception: the brake shall not be applied in case the STM X is known to be isolated, through the corresponding input on the Train Interface.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.6, PDF p.57

10.3.3.6 The emergency brake application shall be released by the STM Control Function when a) the STM X has established the connection to the STM Control Function after a non- final disconnection and the reported STM X state is DA, b) or the level changes to Level 0, 1, 2, 3, c) or the level changes to a Level NTC Y that is not associated to STM X, d) or the mode SN is left with no change of level, e) or the dedicated input on the Train Interface informs the ERTMS/ETCS on-board that the STM X is isolated.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.7, PDF p.57

10.3.3.7 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall accept the reconnection of an STM not considered as in FA state or reporting PO state, except in case of final disconnection on Safety Layers.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.8

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.8, PDF p.57

10.3.3.8 The STM Control Function shall inform the driver that the STM X is not available while all of the following conditions are fulfilled - the level is NTC X, - and (the mode is SN) or (the mode is NL and has been so for at least 5s), - and STM X is known as installed on-board but not available,

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.57

3.2.0 FFFIS - and STM X is not known to be isolated through the corresponding input on the Train Interface.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.3.3.8.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.3.3.8.1, PDF p.58

10.3.3.8.1 Note: the 5s delay on the information to the driver is required because the STM X requests to enter in CS state only after the mode has changed to NL.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.1, PDF p.58

10.4.1.1 The ETCS data transmitted by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board to the STMs shall include a subset of the ETCS Train Data (defined in [1]), as listed below: a) Train category(ies) b) Train length c) Traction / brake parameters d) Maximum train speed e) Loading gauge f) Axle load category g) Traction system(s) accepted by the engine h) Train fitted with airtight system

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.2, PDF p.58

10.4.1.2 The ETCS data transmitted by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board to the STMs shall include a subset of the ETCS Train Data entry input fields (defined in [9]), as listed below: a) Train Type, if applicable for the train

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.3, PDF p.58

10.4.1.3 Note: Extra data for the available STMs are handled in the Specific NTC Data Entry procedure see chapter 10.7.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.4, PDF p.58

10.4.1.4 The traction / brake parameters shall include: a) Equivalent brake build up time for full service brake for the combination of none of the special brakes being used b) Equivalent brake build up time for emergency brake for the combination of none of the special brakes being used c) Traction cut off time d) Brake position e) Brake percentage, if applicable for the train

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.5, PDF p.58

10.4.1.5 The ETCS data transmitted by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board to the STMs shall include a subset of ETCS Additional Data (defined in [1]) as listed below: a) Train Running Number b) ETCS identity c) Adhesion factor d) Date and Time (UTC Time)

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.6, PDF p.59

10.4.1.6 The ETCS data transmitted by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board to the STMs shall include the ETCS National / Default Values (defined in [1])

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.7, PDF p.59

10.4.1.7 The STM Control Function shall transmit the subset of valid ETCS Train Data when the ETCS Train Data is validated.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.7.1, PDF p.59

10.4.1.7.1 Note: ETCS Train Data could be changed and validated from sources different from the driver if acquired from ERTMS/ETCS on-board external sources.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.8, PDF p.59

10.4.1.8 The STM Control Function shall transmit the valid ETCS Additional Data a) when the STM has entered into Configuration (CO) state, and b) when the valid ETCS Additional Data except date / time has changed.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.4.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.4.1.9, PDF p.59

10.4.1.9 The STM Control Function shall transmit the currently used ETCS National / Default Values a) when the STM has entered into Configuration (CO) state, and b) when the currently used ETCS National Values have changed (this also includes the case when the National Values are reset to the Default Values).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.5.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.5.1.1, PDF p.59

10.5.1.1 The STM Control Function shall send the ETCS status data consisting of the current ETCS mode and level (defined in [1]): a) To all connected STMs whenever the ETCS mode or level changes. b) To any STM when the connection to the STM Control Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.6, PDF p.59

10.6 Language used to display information to the driver

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.6.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.6.1.1, PDF p.59

10.6.1.1 The STM Control Function shall transmit the language used to display information to the driver: a) To all connected STMs whenever the language is changed, b) To any STM when the connection to the STM Control Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7, PDF p.59

10.7 Specific NTC Data Entry

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.1.1, PDF p.59

10.7.1.1 The “Specific NTC Data” are the national data that need to be requested to the driver.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.1.2, PDF p.59

10.7.1.2 The STM may use the transmitted ETCS data: ETCS Train Data, ETCS Additional Data and ETCS National Values in order to reduce the entry of “Specific NTC Data” by the driver.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.1.3, PDF p.59

10.7.1.3 All “Specific NTC Data” used by all the different STMs are assigned a unique identity made of NID_STM and Data Identifier.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.1.4, PDF p.60

10.7.1.4 The process to deliver those “Specific NTC Data” to the STM is called “Specific NTC Data Entry”.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.1.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.1.4.1, PDF p.60

10.7.1.4.1 Note: Specific NTC Data Entry is possible at start-up and later on during mission through the Train Data Entry procedure.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.2.1, PDF p.60

10.7.2.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is responsible for the dialogue with the driver during the Specific NTC Data Entry/Validation process, for checking the technical range checks (if configured on-board) and for the transmission of the Specific NTC Data after the driver’s validation.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.2.2, PDF p.60

10.7.2.2 The STM is responsible for checking the content (e.g. range, spares, internal dependency of parameters) of the data. The STM can be exempted of technical range checks if those are configured in the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3, PDF p.60

10.7.3 General requirements

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3.1, PDF p.60

10.7.3.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall offer the possibility to the driver to skip the Specific NTC Data Entry for a STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3.2, PDF p.60

10.7.3.2 The ETCS Train Data as well as the Specific NTC Data might become invalid within the STM at any time due to national requirements. In this case, the STM may request the data from the ETCS by sending the “Specific NTC Data Need”.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3.3, PDF p.60

10.7.3.3 Specific NTC Data can be or become invalid, because: a) the ETCS Train Data Entry/Specific NTC Data Entry procedure has not yet been performed or has been aborted, or b) the driver has skipped the Specific NTC Data Entry for this STM before the STM has sent the “End of Specific NTC Data Entry” to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board, or c) the ETCS Train Data Entry procedure has already been performed by the time the STM has entered into CO state, e.g. the STM has been powered on or restarted during train mission, or d) the ETCS Train Data has changed from sources different from the driver and this change impacts the validity status of the Specific NTC Data, according to national rules, or e) because of STM internal function, e.g. national shunting.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3.4, PDF p.60

10.7.3.4 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board receives the “Specific NTC Data Need” while in FS, LS, SR, OS, UN, TR, PT and SN modes, it shall inform the driver that the national system needs data.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3.5, PDF p.60

10.7.3.5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete this information to the driver when the driver initiates the Train Data entry procedure or when the corresponding STM is considered as failed or when this STM is known to be isolated by TIU “NTC isolation status” input data.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3.6, PDF p.61

10.7.3.6 The STM requests its Specific NTC Data with a “Specific NTC Data Entry request” which shall include for each Specific NTC Data, the following information: the label, optionally a default value, and optionally values for a dedicated keyboard.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3.7, PDF p.61

10.7.3.7 Note: Unless values for a dedicated keyboard are provided or the type of keyboard is configured on-board, an alphanumeric keyboard will by default be used (see document ref [9]).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3.8

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3.8, PDF p.61

10.7.3.8 It shall be possible to configure in the ERTMS/ETCS on-board the following parameters for any STM: 1) The window titles for the NTC data entry, the NTC data validation and the NTC data view windows 2) For each Specific NTC Data Identifier not using a dedicated keyboard: a) The type of keyboard amongst numeric, enhanced numeric and alphanumeric b) If the type of keyboard is numeric or enhanced numeric, whether leading zeros have to be kept and sent to the STM c) The allowed minimum and maximum value, that shall be used by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board with a technical range check

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.3.9

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.3.9, PDF p.61

10.7.3.9 By analogy to the modification/revalidation of ETCS Train data, the [1] requirements 3.14.1.7.3, 3.18.3.3.1 regarding the brake command/release when a movement is detected while modifying or revalidating the Train Data in normal operation after the start of mission shall also apply for the NTC data modification/revalidation.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4, PDF p.61

10.7.4 Specific NTC Data Entry procedure

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.1, PDF p.61

10.7.4.1 As soon as the ETCS Train Data is validated by the driver and if the connected STM is in CO, DE, CS, HS or DA state, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall indicate to the STM the beginning of its Specific NTC Data Entry procedure by sending the START flag.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.2, PDF p.61

10.7.4.2 The ETCS Train Data shall be sent immediately after the START flag.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.3, PDF p.61

10.7.4.3 While a Specific NTC Data Entry is ongoing, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall indicate to the STM the end of its Specific NTC Data Entry procedure by sending the STOP flag when one of the following conditions is fulfilled: a) after having received the “End of Specific NTC Data Entry” from the respective STM, b) at expiration of the timeout specified in 10.7.4.9 for the respective STM, c) when the Train Data Entry procedure is aborted by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board for reasons not related to the STM interface d) the Specific NTC Data Entry for this STM has been skipped by the driver see 10.7.3.1.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.3.1, PDF p.61

10.7.4.3.1 Note: Reasons leading to the abortion of the Train Data entry procedure and not related to the STM interface can be e.g. the cab deactivation, the driver aborting the Train Data entry procedure,...

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.4, PDF p.62

10.7.4.4 Note: ETCS Train Data is also sent without the START and STOP flags outside a Train Data entry procedure, see 10.4.1.7.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.5, PDF p.62

10.7.4.5 Once the STM has received the ETCS Train Data while its Specific NTC Data Entry is ongoing: a) If the STM requires Specific NTC Data, the STM shall send a “Specific NTC Data Entry request” information to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board. b) If the STM doesn’t require Specific NTC Data, the STM shall send an “End of Specific NTC Data Entry” information to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.6, PDF p.62

10.7.4.6 After the ERTMS/ETCS on-board has received the Specific NTC Data Entry request, it shall perform the Specific NTC Data Entry/Validation exchanges with the driver when the driver selects this Specific NTC Data Entry.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.7, PDF p.62

10.7.4.7 Once the Specific NTC Data for an STM has been validated by the driver, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall send the “Specific NTC Data” to this STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.8

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.8, PDF p.62

10.7.4.8 When the STM receives the Specific NTC Data, it checks the data according to its national criteria. Depending on the check result: a) the STM shall send an “End of Specific NTC Data Entry” if the checks are OK and the STM has all the requested data. b) the STM shall send again Specific NTC Data Entry request.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.4.9

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.4.9, PDF p.62

10.7.4.9 For all connected STMs, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall supervise separately a timeout of 10s (TrainDataEntry_STM_Response_Timeout, see chapter 10.3.2.4, O16): a) from sending the ETCS Train Data by the ETCS while the Specific NTC Data Entry procedure is running, until the reception of a Specific NTC Data Entry request or the “End of Specific NTC Data Entry” from the STM and b) from each sending Specific NTC Data by the ETCS until the reception of the Specific NTC Data Entry request or the “End of Specific NTC Data Entry” from the STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.7.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.7.5, PDF p.63

10.7.5 Sequence diagrams for the Specific NTC Data Entry STM A STM B Driver ERTMS/ETCS on-board associated to NTC A Associated to NTC B ETCS Train Data validated Start flag Start flag ETCS Train Data ETCS Train Data Specific NTC Data Entry Request NTC data entry selection window Specific NTC Data Entry Request Buttons for NTC A & B are enabled NTC A selected by the driver Specific NTC Data of NTC A presented to the driver Specific NTC Data for NTC A validated Specific NTC Data values End of Specific NTC Data Entry NTC data entry selection window Buttons for NTC B is enabled Stop flag NTC B selected by the driver Specific NTC Data of NTC B presented to the driver Specific NTC Data for NTC B validated Specific NTC Data values End of Specific NTC Data Entry NTC data entry selection window Buttons for NTC A & B are disabled Stop flag Figure 6 – Specific NTC Data Entry performed

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.63

3.2.0 FFFIS STM A STM B Driver ERTMS/ETCS on-board associated to NTC A associated to NTC B ETCS Train Data validated Start flag Start flag ETCS Train Data ETCS Train Data Specific NTC Data Entry Request NTC data entry selection window Specific NTC Data Entry Request Buttons for NTC A & B are enabled NTC A selected by the driver Specific NTC Data of NTC A presented to the driver Specific NTC Data for NTC A validated Specific NTC Data values End of Specific NTC Data Entry Stop flag NTC data entry selection window Buttons for NTC B is enabled Driver presses “End of data entry“ Stop flag Figure 7 – Specific NTC Data Entry skipped for NTC B

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.64

3.2.0 FFFIS STM A STM B Driver ERTMS/ETCS on-board associated to NTC A associated to NTC B ETCS Train Data validated Start flag Start flag ETCS Train Data ETCS Train Data Specific NTC Data Entry Request NTC data entry selection window Buttons for NTC A & B are Specific NTC Data Entry Request enabled Cab being closed Stop flag Stop flag Figure 8 – Specific NTC Data Entry aborted

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.8

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.8, PDF p.65

10.8 Specific NTC Data View

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.8.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.8.1.1, PDF p.65

10.8.1.1 This procedure shall allow the driver to view the Specific NTC Data View values currently known by the STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.8.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.8.1.2, PDF p.65

10.8.1.2 When the Data View procedure is triggered, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall send to all available STMs a Request for Specific NTC Data View values.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.8.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.8.1.3, PDF p.65

10.8.1.3 Once the STM has received the ETCS Request for Specific NTC Data View values: a) If the STM requires Specific NTC Data View values to be displayed, the STM shall send those Specific NTC Data View values (labels and corresponding values) to the STM Control Function. b) If the STM doesn’t require Specific NTC Data View values to be displayed, the STM shall send a “No Specific NTC Data View values” to the ETCS STM Control Function.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.8.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.8.1.4, PDF p.65

10.8.1.4 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board receives the Specific NTC Data View values, it shall present them to the driver.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.8.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.8.1.5, PDF p.65

10.8.1.5 For all connected STMs, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall supervise separately a timeout of 10s (TrainDataView_STM_Response_Timeout, see chapter 10.3.2.4, N16) from sending the Request for Specific NTC Data View values until the reception of Specific NTC Data View values or the “No Specific Data View values” information from the respective STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.9.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.9.1.1, PDF p.66

10.9.1.1 The STM shall be allowed to send a Test Procedure Permission Request, including a Test Identity, to the STM Control Function.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.9.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.9.1.2, PDF p.66

10.9.1.2 Having received this Test Procedure Permission Request, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall grant Test Procedure Permission when technically suitable.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.9.1.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.9.1.2.1, PDF p.66

10.9.1.2.1 Note: the condition to grant this Test Procedure Permission is specific to ERTMS/ETCS on-board implementation and to the Test Identity requested by the STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.9.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.9.1.3, PDF p.66

10.9.1.3 Having received this Test Procedure Permission, the STM shall perform the test and then report the End of Test Procedure, including test result and optional text message.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.9.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.9.1.3.1, PDF p.66

10.9.1.3.1 Note: the way the test result and text message are displayed is specific to ERTMS/ETCS on-board implementation.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.10.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.10.1.1, PDF p.66

10.10.1.1 This Override procedure (Trip Inhibition, Pass Stop or Pass signal at danger) is specified in order to provide an override for the active system as well as for the system to be activated without applying the brakes (e.g. trip) by both systems.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.10.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.10.1.2, PDF p.66

10.10.1.2 When Override is activated in the active system (ERTMS/ETCS on-board or STM), all on-board systems receive a notification. Each system can then activate and monitor its specific Override procedure limits (e.g. time, distance and/or reception of trackside information) and trip inhibition. Termination of this monitoring is done independently in each system.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.10.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.10.1.3, PDF p.66

10.10.1.3 After a level transition, the activated system is able to immediately have its Override function active. It can then start to supervise the relevant speed for Override under the limits of the activated system according to its specific requirements. The limits may be considered from the location where driver requested Override.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.10.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.10.2.1, PDF p.66

10.10.2.1 In addition to the conditions defined in [1], the ETCS Override status shall be activated when in level NTC, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board has received from the active STM the activation report of its own Override procedure.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.10.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.10.2.2, PDF p.66

10.10.2.2 The ETCS Override function shall be reset each time a new activation report is received from the active STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.10.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.10.2.3, PDF p.66

10.10.2.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall report its Override status (activated or deactivated): a) To any STM with an established connection to the STM Control Function whenever its Override status changes, b) To any connecting STM when the connection to the STM Control Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.10.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.10.2.4, PDF p.67

10.10.2.4 Note: If the Override function is active while in the Mode SN, no speed supervision is performed by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board and all connected STMs except for the active STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.11

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.11, PDF p.67

10.11 Transmission of ETCS airgap messages for STMs

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.11.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.11.1.1, PDF p.67

10.11.1.1 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board receives from an RBC or from a Balise Group as non-infill information airgap data to be transmitted to an NTC, the data shall be transmitted by the STM Control Function to the STM associated to the Level NTC which NID_NTC is contained in this airgap data.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.11.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.11.1.1.1, PDF p.67

10.11.1.1.1 Note: Airgap data received as infill information is not transmitted to STMs.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.11.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.11.1.2, PDF p.67

10.11.1.2 The STM Control Function shall add to the transmitted airgap data the odometer reading of the balise group which transmitted the airgap message, or the odometer reading of the LRBG of the message if it was received from RBC.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.11.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.11.1.3, PDF p.67

10.11.1.3 The odometer reading shall correspond to the estimated odometer value of the location reference of the balise group.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12, PDF p.67

10.12 STM max speed and STM system speed/distance

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1, PDF p.67

10.12.1 After announcement, but before the transition to Level NTC X

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1.1, PDF p.67

10.12.1.1 When an “STM max speed” (V_STMMAX) from STM X in HS state is accepted, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board includes the “STM max speed” in the computation of the MRSP (see [1] 4.5.2) as a speed restriction that shall start at the level transition border.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1.2, PDF p.67

10.12.1.2 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board accepts a new “STM max speed” (V_STMMAX) from STM X, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall replace the previously received “STM max speed” (V_STMMAX) with the new value.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1.3, PDF p.67

10.12.1.3 If the STM X connected or known as installed on-board (see 10.1.1.1) is not available, then the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall consider that “STM max speed” = 0.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1.3.1, PDF p.67

10.12.1.3.1 Note: The purpose of the above requirement is to try to prevent the train to enter in a Level NTC area while this STM is not available.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1.4, PDF p.67

10.12.1.4 When an “STM system speed” (V_STMSYS) together with an “STM system distance” (D_STMSYS) from STM X in HS state is accepted, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard includes the “STM system speed” (V_STMSYS) into the computation of the MRSP (see [1] 4.5.2), as a new speed restriction that shall start at a location “STM system distance” (D_STMSYS) in rear of the level transition border and shall end at the level transition border.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1.5, PDF p.67

10.12.1.5 When an ERTMS/ETCS on-board accepts a new “STM system speed” (V_STMSYS) and “STM system distance” (D_STMSYS) from STM X, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall replace previously received “STM system speed” (V_STMSYS) and “STM system distance” (D_STMSYS) with the new value.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1.6, PDF p.68

10.12.1.6 When the level transition announcement to level NTC X is deleted by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board: a) The “STM system speed” (V_STMSYS) shall be deleted and the supervision of the “STM system speed” (V_STMSYS) shall be stopped by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board; b) The “STM max speed” (V_STMMAX) shall be deleted and the supervision of the “STM max speed” (V_STMMAX) shall be stopped by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1.6.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1.6.1, PDF p.68

10.12.1.6.1 Note: when a new level transition to another level than NTC X is accepted, the previous one is deleted and replaced with this new one.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.1.6.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.1.6.2, PDF p.68

10.12.1.6.2 Note: when a level transition announcement to the same level NTC X is updated (i.e. with a new distance), the "STM system speed" and "STM max speed" are not deleted.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.2, PDF p.68

10.12.2 After the level transition to Level NTC X

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.2.1, PDF p.68

10.12.2.1 Once the train has passed the level transition border, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall supervise the “STM max speed” (V_STMMAX) previously sent by the STM in HS state as ceiling speed until the STM DA state report is received by the ERTMS/ETCS on- board.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.2.2, PDF p.68

10.12.2.2 If the STM is considered to be in FA state by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board after the level transition border, then the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall stop the supervision of “STM max speed” (V_STMMAX).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.12.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.12.2.3, PDF p.68

10.12.2.3 If, for any reasons (e.g. reception of a level transition order or a manual change of level), the level changes to another level than NTC X, the “STM max speed” (V_STMMAX) shall be deleted and the supervision of the “STM max speed” (V_STMMAX) shall be stopped by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.13

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.13, PDF p.68

10.13 Validity of “National Trip Procedure” information

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.13.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.13.1.1, PDF p.68

10.13.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall consider that a National Trip Procedure is active if the “National Trip Procedure” packet has been received within the last 10 seconds (see [1]).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.13.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.13.1.2, PDF p.68

10.13.1.2 Note: if the National Trip Procedure has been released before a level transition, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board will consider it as still active for a maximum of 10 seconds after the reception of the information, but it is assumed that the level transition after the end of this National Trip Procedure won’t happen within this time, as the train is at standstill.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.14

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.14, PDF p.68

10.14 Display of STM failure status

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.14.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.14.1.1, PDF p.68

10.14.1.1 When an STM has reported FA state or is commanded to FA state, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall inform the driver about the failed status of the national system supported by this STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.14.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.14.1.2, PDF p.68

10.14.1.2 When at Start of Mission just after validation of ETCS Train Data an STM known by ERTMS/ETCS on-board configuration to be installed is not in CO, CS, HS or DA state and this STM is not known to be isolated by TIU “NTC isolation status” input data,

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.68

3.2.0 FFFIS ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall inform the driver about the failed status of the national system supported by this STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.15

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.15, PDF p.69

10.15 Interface 'K' Antenna/BTM ID

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.15.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.15.1.1, PDF p.69

10.15.1.1 If the ERTMS/ETCS on-board uses alternative 1 of interface 'K' (see [10]), it shall indicate to all KER (KVB, Ebicab, RSDD) STMs whether it can or not guarantee by its own that the interface 'K' data is coming from the intended Antenna/BTM, when the connection to the STM Control Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.15.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.15.1.2, PDF p.69

10.15.1.2 If ERTMS/ETCS on-board cannot guarantee by its own that the interface 'K' data is coming from the intended Antenna/BTM, the STM Control Function shall inform whether there is an active Antenna/BTM and, if so, which one: a) To all connected KER STMs whenever this information changes, b) To any KER STM when the connection to the STM Control Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.15.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.15.1.3, PDF p.69

10.15.1.3 Note: This information enables an STM using interface 'K' to fulfil a requirement of [10] asking to supervise that the interface 'K' information comes from the intended source.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.16.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.16.1.1, PDF p.69

10.16.1.1 The STM Control Function shall send the BTM alarm data consisting of the BTM alarm status and whether the antenna is within an announced Big Metal Mass track condition: a) To all connected STMs whenever the BTM alarm status changes or whenever an announced Big Metal Mass track condition is entered or exited during a BTM alarm, b) To any STM when the connection to the STM Control Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 10.16.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 10.16.1.2, PDF p.69

10.16.1.2 Note: The ERTMS/ETCS on-board always sends this information over the FFFIS STM interface regardless the alarms are ignored according to [1] 3.12.1 and 3.15.7.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.69

3.2.0 FFFIS 11. TIU AND BIU FUNCTIONS

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 11.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 11.1.1.1, PDF p.70

11.1.1.1 The TIU Function shall transmit train interface inputs status / availability: a) To any STM with an established connection to the TIU Function whenever a train interface inputs status / availability changes. b) To any connecting STM when the connection to the TIU Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 11.1.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 11.1.1.1.1, PDF p.70

11.1.1.1.1 The TIU Function shall transmit train interface commands configuration to any connecting STM when the connection to the TIU Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 11.1.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 11.1.1.2, PDF p.70

11.1.1.2 The BIU Function shall transmit the brake performance parameters to any connecting STM when the connection to the BIU Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 11.1.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 11.1.1.3, PDF p.70

11.1.1.3 The BIU Function shall transmit the brake status / availability: a) To any STM with an established connection to the BIU Function whenever a brake status / availability changes. b) To any connecting STM when the connection to the BIU Function is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 11.1.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 11.1.1.4, PDF p.70

11.1.1.4 When the service brake is commanded by an STM, the STM shall indicate in its request if the service brake shall be backed up automatically by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board with an Emergency Brake command if the service brake fails to be applied.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 11.1.1.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 11.1.1.4.1, PDF p.70

11.1.1.4.1 Note: If it is not the case, this has to be considered as an exception to [1].

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.70

3.2.0 FFFIS 12. ODOMETER FUNCTION

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.1, PDF p.71

12.1.1.1 The FFFIS STM specifies the odometer information to be transmitted from ERTMS/ETCS on-board to all STMs via FFFIS STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.2, PDF p.71

12.1.1.2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall transmit odometer information via the FFFIS STM interface at regular intervals. This information shall include current values of estimated distance, direction, estimated speed, confidence interval of measurement of distance (i.e. minimum and maximum distances) and confidence interval for speed (i.e. minimum and maximum speeds).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.3, PDF p.71

12.1.1.3 Every transmitted odometer information report shall be time stamped. The time base for timestamp shall be the Reference Time obtained from the Safe Time Layer, see 5.2.2. The time in the timestamp shall be the time when the odometer data were valid.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.3.1, PDF p.71

12.1.1.3.1 Justification: this time information allows an STM to extrapolate distance and speed to fit its algorithms and processing cycles.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.4, PDF p.71

12.1.1.4 Positive movement direction is defined as a movements in the forward direction in relation to cab A. It shall be indicated with positive speed and increasing odometer distance values.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.5, PDF p.71

12.1.1.5 Negative movement direction is defined as movements in the backwards direction in relation to cab A. It shall be indicated with negative speed and decreasing odometer distance values.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.5.1, PDF p.71

12.1.1.5.1 Note: Allocation of cab(s) on a specific train is a pure ERTMS/ETCS on-board implementation issue.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.6, PDF p.71

12.1.1.6 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall not reset the odometer distance values as long as the ERTMS/ETCS on-board is powered-on.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.6.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.6.1, PDF p.71

12.1.1.6.1 Justification: The ETCS odometer information is used as a common reference within the FFFIS STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.1.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.1.1.7, PDF p.71

12.1.1.7 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall transmit odometer configuration data (see chapter 12.4) to the STMs.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.2.1.1, PDF p.71

12.2.1.1 Estimated speed, V_Est, shall be the estimated speed as used by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board (also referred as the train speed in [1]).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.2.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.2.1.2, PDF p.71

12.2.1.2 Maximum speed, V_Max, is defined as the most positive speed, i.e. the highest possible physical speed including under-reading amount, in case of movement in positive direction (V_Max = V_Est + |V_ura|). For movements in negative direction

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.71

3.2.0 FFFIS V_Max reports the lowest possible speed in absolute value, i.e. including over-reading amount (V_Max = V_Est + |V_ora|).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.2.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.2.1.3, PDF p.72

12.2.1.3 Minimum speed, V_Min, is defined as the most negative speed, i.e. the lowest possible physical speed including over-reading amount, in case of movement in positive direction (V_Min = V_Est - |V_ora|). For movements in negative direction V_Min reports the highest possible speed in absolute value, i.e. including under-reading amount (V_Min = V_Est - |V_ura|). measured V_Max speed V_Nom V_Min physical speed Figure 9 – Example of transmitted speed information

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.3.1.1, PDF p.72

12.3.1.1 The estimated distance, D_Est, shall be the most probable position of the vehicle in the vehicle coordinate system at the time given in the odometer packet, with reference to the vehicle position at the last reset of the odometry.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.3.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.3.1.2, PDF p.72

12.3.1.2 Note: For any train movement, the most probable distance travelled between any two track positions can be computed as the difference between the measurement values of D_Est at the two positions.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.3.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.3.1.3, PDF p.72

12.3.1.3 D_Max is defined as the most positive position of the vehicle in the vehicle coordinate system at the time given in the odometer packet, with all over- and under-reading amounts accumulated since the last reset of the odometry.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.3.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.3.1.4, PDF p.72

12.3.1.4 D_Min is defined as the most negative position of the vehicle in the vehicle coordinate system at the time given in the odometer packet, with all over- and under-reading amounts accumulated since the last reset of the odometry.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.3.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.3.1.5, PDF p.72

12.3.1.5 The confidence interval shall comply with the relevant requirements specified in [7].

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.3.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.3.1.6, PDF p.72

12.3.1.6 The resolution part of an odometer report shall be given as a parameter in each odometer report from the ETCS Odometer Function. This allows for sensor technologies with varying resolution.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.3.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.3.1.7, PDF p.73

12.3.1.7 Note: The STM can then compute the maximum and minimum travelled distances at the current vehicle position p2 with regards to any reference location p1 by using the resolution information, maximum and minimum distances at the these locations, as follows: max_distance(p1p2) = max(D_Res(p1), D_Res(p2)) + D_Max(p2) – D_Max(p1) min_distance(p1p2) = - max(D_Res(p1), D_Res(p2)) + D_Min(p2) – D_Min(p1)

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.3.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.3.1.8, PDF p.73

12.3.1.8 The distance parameters D_Est, D_Max and D_Min are allowed to wrap when exceeding the value range. The parameters wrap individually.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.4, PDF p.73

12.4 Configuration information

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.4.1.1, PDF p.73

12.4.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board Odometer Function shall transmit performance related information (configuration data) over the FFFIS STM. The transmission shall be repeated to support restarting STMs.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.4.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.4.1.1.1, PDF p.73

12.4.1.1.1 Note: The STM may use the performance-related information (e.g. ageing) to adjust its supervision, e.g. braking curves. Sensor Compute Bus STM Cycle time Bus delay (token cycle) Production delay (including bus delay) Figure 10 – Odometer cycle and delay times

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.4.1.2, PDF p.73

12.4.1.2 Typical cycle time, T_OdoCycle is the typical time for the odometer cycle time between each generating of new odometer data.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.4.1.3, PDF p.73

12.4.1.3 Note: The actual cycle time may well exceed T_OdoCycle.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.4.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.4.1.4, PDF p.73

12.4.1.4 Maximum production delay time, T_OdoMaxProd is the maximum ageing of odometer data from when the data was true until the data is available on the bus. This shall include clock synchronisation inaccuracy of the Odometer Function.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 12.4.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 12.4.1.5, PDF p.73

12.4.1.5 Note: The actual production delay time should not exceed T_OdoMaxProd.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.73

3.2.0 FFFIS 13. DRIVER MACHINE INTERFACE FUNCTION

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.1.1.1, PDF p.74

13.1.1.1 The DMI Function allows the driver to directly interact with the ERTMS/ETCS on-board for what regards the national information related to the default window. That means that all inputs from the driver to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board and all outputs from the ERTMS/ETCS on-board to the driver in the default window are controlled by this function.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.1.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.1.1.2, PDF p.74

13.1.1.2 The DMI Function shall provide the unified DMI and the customisable DMI services.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.1.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.1.1.3, PDF p.74

13.1.1.3 An STM designed for usage with a customisable DMI provides a set of configuration data for its default window as part of its product documentation as described in chapter 13.5. The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall be configurable to store this information and serve the STM DMI requests according to this configuration. The customisable DMI service shall be used, when configuration data for a customisable DMI layout are stored in the ERTMS/ETCS on-board for the NID_STM of the STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.1.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.1.1.4, PDF p.74

13.1.1.4 An STM designed to use the unified DMI provides no configuration data as part of its product documentation. The unified DMI service shall be used, when no configuration data for a customisable DMI layout is stored in the ERTMS/ETCS on-board for the NID_STM of the STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.1.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.1.1.5, PDF p.74

13.1.1.5 Note: Unconfigurable parts of the DMI functions shall be handled in the same way by the unified and the customisable DMI services.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2, PDF p.74

13.2 General requirements regarding DMI Function

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2.1.1, PDF p.74

13.2.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall only allow the active STM to communicate with the driver.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2.1.2, PDF p.74

13.2.1.2 When the STM is no more active (see 4.1.1.3), the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete all DMI objects controlled by this STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2.1.3, PDF p.74

13.2.1.3 When the connection between an STM and the DMI Function is disconnected, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete all the DMI objects controlled by this STM (including preliminary requests) after a timeout of 2 seconds.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2.1.3.1, PDF p.74

13.2.1.3.1 Justification: The timeout of 2 seconds is to give the STM the chance to re-establish the connection.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2.1.4, PDF p.74

13.2.1.4 When the connection between the active STM and the DMI Function is lost and re- established within the timeout of 2 seconds, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete all the DMI objects controlled by the STM when the DMI connection to the STM is established.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2.1.5, PDF p.75

13.2.1.5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall be able to receive and store preliminary request for DMI objects from an STM being in HS state and display them immediately after having received the DA state report.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2.1.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2.1.5.1, PDF p.75

13.2.1.5.1 Note: The sending of preliminary request is to allow the DMI Function to prepare in background the information to be presented to the driver once the STM switches to DA state. Therefore, the STM should send all DMI objects that needs to be displayed after the change to DA as preliminary DMI request.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2.1.6, PDF p.75

13.2.1.6 When an STM reports PO, CS or FA, or is considered as failed, the ERTMS/ETCS on- board shall delete all preliminary requests for DMI objects from this STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.2.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.2.1.7, PDF p.75

13.2.1.7 If the ETCS train speed is configured not to be displayed for an STM while the ERTMS/ETCS on-board is in SN mode (see chapter 13.5.1.1.7), the ERTMS/ETCS on- board shall inhibit the display of the ETCS train speed only once the DA state report is received from this STM by the STM Control Function.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.3.1.1, PDF p.75

13.3.1.1 The DMI Function shall be allowed to use up to four DMI channels. Each channel shall correspond to one connection.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.3.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.3.1.2, PDF p.75

13.3.1.2 At most one DMI channel shall be active, only this one shall be used for the communication related to DMI objects with the DMI Function at application level.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.3.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.3.1.3, PDF p.75

13.3.1.3 Note 1: Connections corresponding to the inactive DMI channels may however remain open.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.3.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.3.1.3.1, PDF p.75

13.3.1.3.1 Note 2: The ERTMS/ETCS on-board may report a DMI channel as active even if no interaction with the driver is possible, e.g. when no cab is active.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.3.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.3.1.4, PDF p.75

13.3.1.4 At the time the active DMI channel changes, the DMI Function shall delete all the DMI objects controlled by the STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1, PDF p.75

13.4.1 DMI object identities

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.1, PDF p.75

13.4.1.1 The DMI objects indicators and buttons used by the different STMs are assigned a unique object identity made of NID_STM and Indicator/Button Identifier.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.2, PDF p.75

13.4.1.2 The STM Identity is implicitly provided by the STM by its announced NID_STM (and repeated in each message header according to the language).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.3, PDF p.75

13.4.1.3 The Indicator/Button Identifier is provided by the STM as part of the corresponding Indicator/Button request.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.4, PDF p.75

13.4.1.4 The Indicator/Button Identifier is used by the STM to be able to change the state of objects and to move or remove them. The Button Identifier is also used by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board to transmit the button events to the STM. If the customisable DMI service is used, it is also used to define the properties of the object.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.5, PDF p.76

13.4.1.5 All icons (bitmap symbols) used by the different STMs using a customisable DMI are assigned an icon identity made of NID_STM and Icon Identifier.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.6, PDF p.76

13.4.1.6 An Icon Identifier can be provided by the STM as part of the corresponding Indicator/Button request.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.7, PDF p.76

13.4.1.7 All sounds (wave form for audible information) used by the different STMs using a customisable DMI are assigned a unique sound identity made of NID_STM and Sound Identifier.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.8, PDF p.76

13.4.1.8 A Sound Identifier can be provided by the STM as part of the corresponding sound request.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.9, PDF p.76

13.4.1.9 For specifying the position of DMI objects, Position Identifiers are used.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.10

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.10, PDF p.76

13.4.1.10 If the unified DMI service is used, the Position Identifier specifies an area of the ETCS layout as defined in [9].

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.1.11

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.1.11, PDF p.76

13.4.1.11 If the customisable DMI service is used, the Position Identifier and the NID_STM are used to define the position in cell coordinates and size as specified in the configuration data for this STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.2.1, PDF p.76

13.4.2.1 The DMI Function shall display a text message when requested by the STM. The text message request shall consist of a Text Identifier, a string of text to be shown to the driver, a display attribute and a possible request for driver acknowledgement.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.2.2, PDF p.76

13.4.2.2 The DMI Function shall report to the STM the acknowledgement of text messages (which were required to be acknowledged) from the driver referencing the corresponding Text Identifier.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.2.3, PDF p.76

13.4.2.3 The DMI Function shall delete a text message when requested by the active STM. The request shall reference the Text Identifier of the text message to be deleted.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.2.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.2.3.1, PDF p.76

13.4.2.3.1 Note: The acknowledgement does not lead to the end of the display of a text message.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.2.4, PDF p.76

13.4.2.4 If the STM requests a text message with the same Text Identifier as a not yet deleted text message, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall delete the original text message and display the new requested text message.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.2.5, PDF p.76

13.4.2.5 The display attribute specifies the colour of the text, its background colour, the flashing mode and the group of text messages.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.2.6, PDF p.76

13.4.2.6 The flashing mode specifies if the slow, fast or no flashing and if normal or counterphase flashing shall be used.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.3.1, PDF p.76

13.4.3.1 An Indicator is a DMI object for display of information without input.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.3.2, PDF p.76

13.4.3.2 The STM shall request the display of an Indicator by means of the following definition:

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.76

3.2.0 FFFIS a) its Indicator Identifier, b) an optional Icon Identifier, c) an optional caption text, d) a Position Identifier, e) a display attribute.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.3.3, PDF p.77

13.4.3.3 The Icon Identifier shall be used by the DMI Function in case of the customisable DMI service to retrieve from the configuration data the corresponding icon attached to an Indicator/Button object.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.3.4, PDF p.77

13.4.3.4 The display attribute shall specify the background colour and the flashing mode for the whole Indicator and the display colour of the caption text.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.3.5, PDF p.77

13.4.3.5 The flashing mode specifies if the slow, fast or no flashing and if normal or counterphase flashing shall be used.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.4.1, PDF p.77

13.4.4.1 Buttons are a pure functional extension of Indicators. All requirements of chapter 13.4.3 shall apply to Buttons, by replacing "Indicator" with "Button".

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.4.2, PDF p.77

13.4.4.2 The extension is the transmission of Button events from the DMI Function to STM. The DMI Function shall make a distinction between push event (transition from Button not pressed to pressed state) and release event (opposite transition).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.4.3, PDF p.77

13.4.4.3 The DMI Function shall report Button push and release events to the STM and shall timestamp those event reports to reflect the sequence of events.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.4.4, PDF p.77

13.4.4.4 The DMI Function shall use the Reference Time (see chapter 5.2.2) for timestamping the Button events reports.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.5.1, PDF p.77

13.4.5.1 STM shall request a Sound by means of the following definition: a) an optional Sound Identifier, b) only in case of a unified DMI and a Sound to be generated, a sequence of segments defined by a duration and an associated frequency,

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 3.2.0

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 3.2.0, PDF p.77

3.2.0 FFFIS Freq. Time Figure 11: Example of sound definition c) an indication if the Sound has to be repeated continuously or not or to be stopped.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.5.2, PDF p.78

13.4.5.2 The Sound Identifier shall be used by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board in case of the customisable DMI service to retrieve from the configuration data the corresponding sound.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.5.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.5.3, PDF p.78

13.4.5.3 The Sound Identifier shall be used by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board in both DMI services to stop the generation of a Sound, if requested by the STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.5.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.5.4, PDF p.78

13.4.5.4 The DMI Function shall be able to manage two STM requests for Sounds at the same time.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.5.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.5.4.1, PDF p.78

13.4.5.4.1 Note: This will allow an STM to request a long Sound and a short Sound simultaneously.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.6

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.6, PDF p.78

13.4.6 Supervision information

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.6.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 13.4.6.1, PDF p.78

13.4.6.1 There shall be two sets of supervision information: a) Speed and distance values b) Colours and display modes

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 13.4.6.2

15.1.1.2 The allowed text font height range for the configurable elements of the DMI layout of an STM using the customisable DMI service shall be from 8 to 60 cells.

3.2.0 FFFIS 16. VERSION MANAGEMENT

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.1.1.1, PDF p.86

16.1.1.1 The version of the FFFIS STM defines unambiguously the mandatory interface functions that ensure technical exchangeability between ERTMS/ETCS on-board and STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.1.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.1.1.2, PDF p.86

16.1.1.2 During the life time of the FFFIS STM there may be several versions of the FFFIS STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.1.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.1.1.3, PDF p.86

16.1.1.3 The objective of this section is to define requirements applicable to ERTMS/ETCS on- board equipment and to STM, when different versions of the FFFIS STM have been defined.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.2, PDF p.86

16.2 Identification/evolution of the versions

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.2.1.1, PDF p.86

16.2.1.1 The evolution of the versions of the FFFIS STM shall be sequential, i. e. there shall only be a direct upgrade of an existing version and no branch is accepted.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.2.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.2.1.2, PDF p.86

16.2.1.2 The version of the FFFIS STM shall be identified by a number which complies with the following: a) Each Version Number will have the following format: X.Y, where X and Y are any number between 0 and 255 (examples: 2.0, 3.0, 4.2). b) The first number (X) distinguishes not compatible versions. c) The second number (Y) indicates compatibility within a version X. d) If the first number of two versions is the same, that indicates that those versions are compatible, independently of the second number (e. g. version 4.5 is compatible with 4.3, 4.14).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.2.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.2.1.3, PDF p.86

16.2.1.3 The “FFFIS STM version number X or Y” is incremented only when the functionality of the FFFIS STM changes.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.3.1.1, PDF p.86

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.3.1.2, PDF p.87

16.3.1.2 The STM shall support and send one and only one “FFFIS STM version number”, which is the highest one amongst those included in the “legal backward compatibility envelope”, as defined in table 16.3.1.1.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.3.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.3.1.3, PDF p.87

16.3.1.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall support any of the “FFFIS STM version numbers X” included in the “legal backward compatibility envelope”, as defined in table 16.3.1.1.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.3.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.3.1.4, PDF p.87

16.3.1.4 All nodes/functions of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall support the same “FFFIS STM version numbers” and shall therefore send the same “FFFIS STM version number”, when opening a connection with a given STM (see section 7.1.2).

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.3.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.3.1.5, PDF p.87

16.3.1.5 When a connection is successfully established with a “FFFIS STM version number X” lower than the highest STM version numbers X included in the “legal backward compatibility envelope”, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall apply the corresponding set of requirements as per section 16.4, in order to ensure backward compatibility between the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment and the STM.

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.4

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.4, PDF p.87

16.4 Management of older FFFIS STM versions by ERTMS/ETCS on- board

SUBSET-035 v3.2.0 — clause 16.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-035 v3.2.0, clause 16.4.1.1, PDF p.87

16.4.1.1 The “FFFIS STM version number” introduced in this version of the SUBSET-035 is the starting point of the “legal backward compatibility envelope”, which means that whether an ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment supports a “FFFIS STM version number X” lower than the one introduced in this version of the SUBSET-035 is supplier specific and outside the scope of this document.

SUBSET-058 v3.2.0 — clause 3.1.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-058 v3.2.0, clause 3.1.1.1, PDF p.23

3.1.1.1 The FFFIS STM Application Layer specifies data formats that shall be used in the communication between Specific Transmission Module STM and ERTMS/ETCS on- board.

SUBSET-058 v3.2.0 — clause 3.1.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-058 v3.2.0, clause 3.1.1.2, PDF p.23

3.1.1.2 The boundary to lower layers is the Safe Time Layer.

SUBSET-058 v3.2.0 — clause 3.1.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-058 v3.2.0, clause 3.1.1.3, PDF p.23

3.1.1.3 The boundary to higher layer is the application processes within the STM and the ERTMS/ETCS on-board.

SUBSET-058 v3.2.0 — clause 3.1.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-058 v3.2.0, clause 3.1.1.4, PDF p.23

3.1.1.4 The scope of this document is the Application Layer only.

SUBSET-058 v3.2.0 — clause 3.1.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-058 v3.2.0, clause 3.1.1.5, PDF p.23

3.1.1.5 The transmitted message is embedded in a safety protocol structure as defined by Safe Time Layer and Safe Link Layer. (See [5] and [6]). Message Body Header Application Layer with Packets Com- Time Safe Time Layer mand Stamp Explicit Com- Safe Link Layer CRC Header mand Profibus FDL Layer Header CRC Figure 1: FFFIS STM Layers 3.2.0 4. INTRODUCTION

Citation: SUBSET-058 v3.2.0, clause 4.1, PDF p.24
